Excellent idea, i will give it a go and get back with the results! @chrislusf

I managed to resolve the conflicts by hand, but I am not 100% sure it's right. Would you be please so kind and rebase the branch yourself in order to have "official" foundationdb PR branch?

FYI i tried to to run `make test-container` in `test/foundationdb` and it is also failing

for my use case it is crucial that seaweedfs filer runs on foundationdb and with s3 gateway, thinking about the way how to tackle this. do you think i should fix all the compilation and test issues? or are you willing to fix `add-foundation-db` branch so that `make test-container` works (and possibly other tests) and then i proceed with my usecase?

Here is the patch as promised, in case anyone is interested.

To test it locally:

1. install docker, docker-compose v2.35.1+, aws cli
1. cd test/foundationdb

hello @chrislusf, I deployed seaweeds with fdb support and encountered weird issues, so I double checked my patch and the ci-e2e tests and found out that I was happy too early as it does not work correctly.

The issue is that using aws cli the tests are seemingly able to create buckets, upload file and even download file, but after the upload when I run weed shell, s3.bucket.list shows no buckets and ls/tree shows no files and on my deployment the filer log is filled with many errors:

```
I1106 10:18:16.370504 filer_notify.go:105 metadata log write failed /topics/.system/log/2025-11-06/08-33.4a71b156: AssignVolume: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to find writable volumes for collection: replication:000 ttl: error: No writable volumes and no free volumes left for {"replication":{},"ttl":{"Count":0,"Unit":0},"preallocate":1073741824,"version":3}

I1106 10:18:37.899237 filer_notify.go:105 metadata log write failed /topics/.system/log/2025-11-06/08-33.4a71b156: AssignVolume: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to find writable volumes for collection: replication:000 ttl: error: No writable volumes and no free volumes left for {"replication":{},"ttl":{"Count":0,"Unit":0},"preallocate":1073741824,"version":3}
```
I tried to switch from fdb back to ldb2 and re-run the ci-e2e tests (from test/foundationdb folder) and with ldb2 everything works correctly (as expected), s3.bucket.list shows buckets, ls/tree also shows expected entries.

So after all I think that foundationdb_store does not work correctly.

I would like to kindly ask you if you have time/capacity to give me some support in order to debug this issue. I am doing PoC of quite large deployment involving SeaweedFS and at this time this issue is quite a hurdle to achieve multi-region/DR for the whole solution. I am by no means expert of SeaweedFS or go, so I don't see big chance to debug it myself.

If you don't have time/capacity to help me with this, please let me know as I would have to find alternative solution for my deployment.

FYI I also tried to list keys in fdb and actually I saw a lot of SeaweedFS related keys, so the connection and communication with fdb on the base level works. Really hope we will sort this out somehow.

FYI#2 Right now I tried to rebase the changes to 3.99 and it exhibits the same weird behaviour in the sense that s3.bucket.list and ls/tree return nothing but with ldb2 it shows buckets and files correctly.

Is is expected with filer remote metadata stores to s3.bucket.list and ls/tree to show nothing? I don't think so, but I might be wrong.
FYI#3 It seems only listing of entries from fdb does not work! I can `cd /buckets/test-fdb-bucket` and even `cat /buckets/test-fdb-bucket/test-file.txt` but `ls` or `tree` return nothing.
